feedback: Overall assessment: The answer contains multiple factual errors and omits the core components of RLHF as used in current ML practice. Major issues: it incorrectly expands RLHF as "Reactive Learning from Human Feedback" (the correct term is Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) and frames the method primarily as a robotics technique involving humans pressing buttons on a controller. While the idea of learning from human feedback is broadly correct, the answer fails to describe the standard RLHF pipeline (supervised fine-tuning, collecting human preference comparisons, training a reward model, and then RL fine-tuning such as PPO) and instead gives a misleading, narrow example. Specific guidance by rubric: Accuracy — the answer makes fundamental factual errors (wrong name, misleading application) and thus is largely inaccurate. Comprehensiveness — it provides very little of the relevant information and misses key steps and use cases. Relevance/coherence — parts are on-topic (learning from human feedback / relation to reinforcement learning) but much of the content is irrelevant or overly specific to a misguided robotics scenario, reducing coherence. Depth — the explanation is superficial and lacks the multi-stage process, technical mechanisms (reward modeling, policy optimization), and common use cases (e.g., aligning language models). To improve: correct the name, present the typical RLHF workflow (SFT, preference data, reward model, RL fine-tuning), mention common algorithms (e.g., PPO) and typical applications (aligning large language models), and avoid implying the method is primarily about humans pressing buttons on robots.
